🃏 Pathfinder Spell Planner

"Four slots, four Heals. The font provides."

Plan a Pathfinder Second Edition caster's spells the Remaster way: fill prepared slots from your tradition, spellbook, or familiar, build a repertoire rank by rank with signature spells, and see your cantrips, focus spells, and Focus Points. Granted spells from your bloodline, mystery, muse, or school fill in by themselves.

How spellcasting works in Pathfinder 2e

Every Pathfinder caster draws on one of four traditions (arcane, divine, occult, or primal) and casts with spell slots by rank, 1st to 10th. A spell cast from a higher slot than its own rank is heightened. Cantrips and focus spells don't use slots and are always heightened to half your level, rounded up.

Prepared casters

Clerics and druids prepare from the whole common list of their tradition each morning; a wizard prepares from their spellbook and a witch from the spells their familiar knows. Each slot holds one spell, and the same spell can fill more than one. A wizard gets one more slot a rank (and one more cantrip) for spells from their school's curriculum, and a cleric's divine font adds 4 slots of heal or harm at their highest rank (5 at level 5, 6 at level 15).

Spontaneous casters

Bards, oracles, and sorcerers know a repertoire and cast any spell in it with a slot of its rank. They learn one spell for each slot they gain, at that rank, so a spell learned at 1st rank can't be cast from a 3rd-rank slot unless it's learned again there, or unless it's a signature spell: from level 3, one spell per rank heightens freely. A sorcerer's bloodline adds its sorcerous gift spells as one of each rank's picks; an oracle's mystery and a bard's muse add theirs on top.

Focus spells

Bloodline, revelation, school, composition, hex, order, domain, and devotion spells are focus spells. Your pool holds one Focus Point for each one you know, up to 3; casting one spends a point, and 10 minutes of Refocus brings one back. Focus cantrips (compositions and hexes that are cantrips) cost nothing.

Works with

Build the character in the Character Builder and pick them here: their tradition, spell DC, and feats come along. Look up any spell in the Pathfinder spell list, and keep the party's numbers in the Party Tracker.
